correctness.rationale: Full symbolic proof: length-n factor identifies the entire word when n<=k; otherwise k-factor incidence determines the (k-1)-prefix; palindrome symmetry makes the centered parity-matched j-factor the unique odd-count palindromic factor. For n<=3k this and the mirrored prefix cover all but at most one symmetric letter pair, which length-one counts determine. At n=3k+1 the two explicit binary two-marker palindromes have identical factor multiplicities at every order j<=k because no observed factor sees both markers and each marker contributes once in every offset. Independent exhaustive finite scripts passed for q=2 k<=7, q=3 k<=4, q=4 k<=3.

value.rationale: The exact linear 3k+1 first-ambiguity threshold uniformly over every positive factor order gives a natural symmetric-source reconstruction theorem and an explicit count-based decoder. It extends beyond the existing finite order-three boundary and the unrestricted 2k threshold, and a sharp two-marker construction proves optimality. This is an all-parameter structural result rather than a routine finite census; no general nonpalindromic reconstruction claim is made.
